turnaround_reason: INSP fell from ~$147 to ~$64 after cutting 2026 guidance on reimbursement/coding challenges with its new Inspire 5 system and intensifying competition (GLP-1s, rival hypoglossal-nerve devices). It is basing after a +20% 30-day bounce as management points to sequential recovery in 2H as coding clarity improves.
bullish_points: Clean balance sheet: ~$321M cash vs only ~$29M debt, and still GAAP-profitable (15% net margin) — rare for a beaten-down growth medtech
86% gross margins and an installed base / recurring procedure model give real operating leverage if volumes reaccelerate
Net insider buying (net +32k shares, 18 purchases) signals some management conviction at these levels
High short interest (~20% of float, 5.51 ratio) provides squeeze potential on any guidance stabilization
Management guides to sequential 2H recovery as Inspire 5 coding/reimbursement clarity increases
bearish_points: Guidance was cut up to 10% on reimbursement and WISeR-program headwinds — the core growth engine has stalled (Q1 revenue +1.6%)
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are a genuine structural threat to the sleep-apnea device addressable market
Territory contraction and a pivot to supporting existing accounts signal a retreat from the high-growth expansion story
Multiple analysts (JPM, RBC, Mizuho) cut targets; a share/ESOP shelf registration adds potential dilution overhang
Basing, not confirmed recovering — the bounce could be a lower high within a downtrend
catalyst: Coding/reimbursement clarity on Inspire 5 driving a return to double-digit revenue growth, confirmed on 2H 2026 prints
suggested_trade: Spot only, small; wait for a Q3 print that confirms sequential revenue re-acceleration before adding
key_risk: Reimbursement/coding headwinds persist and GLP-1 competition compresses the addressable market, turning the 'temporary' guidance cut into a structural de-rate
would_skip_if: Q3 revenue growth stays low-single-digit or guidance is cut again — the reimbursement fix has to show up in the numbers first
